goal: Make the coordinator consume the verifier attestation before projecting a rework verdict: kept findings alone become Executor work, refuted claims are archived on the record, an all-refuted verdict buys exactly one reviewer redispatch, a repeated refuted anchor stops for the user, and verifier failure keeps every finding.

acceptance.assertion: Meet S3 in docs/specs/review-verifier-eval.spec.md, driving real submitted verdicts through the coordinator rather than asserting prompt text: after a rework verdict validates and before any request_rework projection, the coordinator returns a verification_ready state carrying one exact foreground verifier dispatch (prompt verbatim, receipt-bound submit_verification, single-use reservation, artifacts still frozen, pass verdicts never verified); a valid verification projects kept findings only and records each refuted claim in verifier_refutations with its counter-path plus a verification history event with checked and refuted counts; an all-refuted verdict synthesizes no pass and issues exactly one new Review reservation whose coordinator-built prompt carries the counter-evidence, and the redispatched verdict is verified again; a repeated anchor refuted for the same snapshot blocks submission and parks the task for a literal-user dispute decision with zero Executor work projected; verifier timeout, dispatch failure, malformed output, or receipt mismatch records the failure and projects all findings without automatic retry; the review_verifier config switch defaults off until the S1 baseline exists and off reproduces today's projection exactly; records without verifier fields parse and settle unchanged on both hosts. The S3 item 7 escalation check also applies: a Host-side Jev-style classifier (invoked by the Host, never by the runtime) scores each refuted finding's true-positive probability from its trigger, caller chain, and counter-path, recorded with its threshold version in the verification event; a score meeting the code-owned threshold escalates to the literal-user dispute stop instead of archiving, a below-threshold score archives, classifier failure archives with the failure recorded, and the classifier never refutes or keeps a finding by itself, never affects kept findings, and takes its threshold from S1 baseline data under the S1 eval gate.
